notes: T545 — three store writers take no lock (the brief's title): the audit found FIVE, not three. The brief's survey counted cmdAssert as correct (it does take lockStore), but cmdAssert reads the store BEFORE the lock and writes the STALE snapshot under it — the identical lost-update shape as cmdTell. cmdSync/writeSyncData (raw read → raw whole-file rename, no lock at all) is a fifth writer the survey missed. All five now follow the documented lock→read→modify→write→unlock order (writeStateLocked under the held flock): (1) the startup migration block in main, (2) cmdTell, (3) cmdAssert, (4) cmdStanding (registerStanding's two writeState calls + persistStandingState's raw surgery, now serialized by one lock at the top of cmdStanding), (5) cmdSync. RED reproduced against the pre-fix binary: 10 concurrent tells → counter=2 (want 11), 5 ledger lines, all five D001 (4 directives minted-but-lost); a claim injected while tell was parked between read and write was REVERTED (status back to dispatchable); a done close injected while a migration-triggering `status` was parked was REVERTED. GREEN against the fixed binary: all five control arms in tools/regression-managent-concurrency.sh pass (N tells → N distinct ids + counter+N; tell-vs-claim survives; migration-vs-done survives; standing+set both survive; null single tell unchanged). Design decision on the brief's 'narrow write' option: locking was chosen, NOT a narrow counter write — the counter lives inside _sys in the same file, so a narrow write would need the raw string surgery that already produced the _standing/_sync defects; under a lock spanning read→write the whole-file write reverts nothing (no concurrent writer can land between). T544 linkage: arm 2 demonstrates the exact revert mechanism that could erase a `done`'s model attribution, so the brief's candidate cause for the 152 null-model rows is MECHANISM-ESTABLISHED but NOT PROVEN for the historical rows — T544 must run its own forensics against the historical store. Sibling defect found but OUT OF SCOPE: serializeState drops the `_standing` and `_sync` keys (parser skips `_`-prefixed keys, serializer never emits them), so any store write from another command erases them until the next standing/sync run — the standing trigger priors read 0 after any other store write; a first-class _standing in StateMap is the real fix. Also: cmdTell now verifies the directive is readable back from the ledger after writing (directiveIsReadable) and fails loudly if not — a directive must never be silently lost.
